scope: Stable MATLAB-like v1.0 target subset; not complete MATLAB compatibility

features.feature: Lossless tokens, trivia, identifiers, numbers, text literals, keywords, operators, and bounded command forms
features.limits: Single and double quoted literals preserve distinct character-array and string-array runtime kinds. Hexadecimal and binary integer literals are consumed as one token and support exact smallest-unsigned inference plus u8/u16/u32/u64 and s8/s16/s32/s64 suffixes with overflow and invalid-digit diagnostics. The active v1.3 tree supports documented clear command forms and a statement-leading ! shell escape; the latter preserves the rest of one physical line and lowers to the capability-gated system builtin. Arbitrary MATLAB command syntax remains outside the target subset.

features.feature: Expression precedence with delayed call/index and member resolution
features.limits: MATLAB-compatible unary power precedence and left-associated ^ and .^ chains are supported. Within matrix and cell concatenation, whitespace before + or - with no whitespace after the sign starts a new unary-signed element, so [1 -2] has two elements while [1 - 2] is one subtraction expression. Runtime workspace values can shadow statically bound callables; nested callable arguments inherit an enclosing array's end context, while a concrete shadowing array creates the nearer context. Production method/object dispatch and anonymous closures are supported through the bytecode VM. Anonymous-function text parsing, computed-string lazy source loading, and remaining uncommon MATLAB call/index shadowing combinations remain open.

features.feature: for, parfor-as-serial, while, if, switch, try/catch, break, continue, return
features.limits: Top-level commas delimit one-line if/switch/for/while forms while nested expression commas retain argument and array meaning. switch case expressions may be scalar values or Cells whose elements are tested in order. parfor executes serially; typed regions accept only structured eligible control flow; no finally construct exists in MATLAB or MParser.

features.feature: Local and nested functions, positional/repeating/name-value arguments, nargin/nargout, and multiple outputs
features.limits: Function call frames and argument/output behavior are shared across the interpreter, VM, C ABI generation 2, C++ source API 1.3, and machine protocol 1.1 projections. Nested functions use qualified lexical identities, exact semantic free-variable capture, shared updates while the parent frame is active, sibling lookup, and active-scope named handles. A nested-function handle that escapes after its lexical parent returns is diagnosed because retained shared-workspace closure lifetime is not implemented. An independently compiled native callback or plugin ABI is not currently exposed.

features.feature: Cross-file source loading, paths, packages, private functions, and class folders
features.limits: MATLAB path precedence and shadowing are implemented for the declared subset, not every toolbox or built-in precedence case.

features.feature: Dense core numeric/logical scalar, vector, matrix, N-dimensional, and complex shape/index semantics
features.limits: The v1.2 development runtime represents dense logical, double, single, all eight fixed-width integer classes, and complex double/single values with column-major shapes through the interpreter, VM, embedding API, and machine protocol. Exact int64/uint64 values combine with scalar double through a platform-independent dyadic path that preserves bits above flintmax across both operand orders, N-dimensional expansion, arithmetic, division, mod/rem, software-emulated binary80 intermediate rounding, integer conversion, non-finite values, and saturation. Typed/native numeric kernels remain deliberately double-specialized and use guards plus transactional fallback for other classes or complex values. Sparse, half, fixed-point, GPU, categorical, table, and complex integer storage are not represented. Object arrays use the separate CLASS-006 contract.

features.feature: Logical indexing, colon/end indexing, indexed growth, and deletion
features.limits: A(:) always produces a numel(A)-by-1 result while ordinary linear subscripts retain the documented vector-orientation rules. Typed/native coverage is narrower than VM correctness and falls back under guards.

features.feature: Distinct UTF-16 character arrays and string arrays with shared shape, indexing, mutation, numeric conversion, and formatting contracts
features.limits: The frozen v1.2 behavior covers quote/empty distinctions, UTF-8/UTF-16 boundaries, indexing, mutation, concatenation, expansion, transforms, conversions, predicates, missing strings, class properties, and CLI formatting. The active v1.3 tree additionally disambiguates whitespace-separated character literals from transpose; provides shape-aware lower/upper/strtrim, num2str, int2str, class-aware mat2str, isolated numeric str2num, strsplit, overlapping UTF-16 strfind/strrep across scalar, string-array, and Cell inputs; compares shaped Cell arrays of text scalars through strcmp/strcmpi with scalar expansion; implements shape-preserving contains/startsWith/endsWith with multiple patterns and IgnoreCase; and provides a portable regexp subset through shared HIR/VM handlers. Binary text, Unicode normalization and locale-wide non-ASCII case folding, Pattern objects, the complete MATLAB regular-expression dialect, complete text function families, tables/categorical values, and typed/native lowering remain open.

features.feature: First-class scalar and N-dimensional missing arrays with shape-preserving indexing, mutation, transforms, conversion, and transport
features.limits: The runtime distinguishes the internal zero-element absent-result sentinel from language-visible missing values. Bare missing and missing() produce a storable 1-by-1 seed; Matrix/MatrixRow concatenation produces shaped missing arrays, including [missing missing] as 1-by-2. Indexing, growth, deletion, transpose, reshape, permute, squeeze, repmat, generic N-dimensional flip, equality, validation, C/C++ transport, and machine protocol preserve shape without materializing an element payload. The active v1.3 ordering layer also sorts and deduplicates billion-element shape-only missing arrays, with explicit missing-distinct policy and index outputs when requested. Datetime, categorical, table, and typed/native missing lowering remain open.

features.feature: Row-structured N-dimensional Cell construction, scalar brace reads/writes, varargin, and varargout-like values
features.limits: Semicolon-delimited Cell literal rows remain explicit through Parser, HIR, bytecode, interpreter, and VM and are vertically concatenated under ordinary dimension checks; empty cells, array-valued elements, and ragged-row diagnostics are covered without flattening. Brace selections produce comma-separated lists that expand in function arguments, output lists, and numeric or Cell literals; bytecode carries requested brace output arity and reports mismatches deterministically. Shared indexing/mutation and varargs remain supported. The active v1.3 tree adds iscell, iscellstr, N-dimensional num2cell/cell2mat, synchronous cellfun, and shape-preserving arrayfun with multiple callback outputs, UniformOutput, and ErrorHandler through the shared dynamic invoker. Every MATLAB comma-list distribution context is not implied.

features.feature: Ordered scalar structures, static/dynamic fields, fieldnames, isfield, rmfield, and isstruct
features.limits: Scalar structures use the same canonical element/schema representation as structure arrays. The shared lvalue transaction creates a missing structure root for direct or indexed member paths, grows indexed gaps, aligns field schemas during copy-back, and supports nested and dynamic fields.

features.feature: Structure arrays and comma-separated field lists
features.limits: v0.71 established array storage and field lists; v0.72 adds nested S(index).field copy-back, indexed intermediate growth, and schema extension. The active v1.3 tree extends this to undefined roots such as s(1).a and multi-dimensional indexed creation, and adds dimension-aware struct2cell and cell2struct with field-order preservation. Bulk field assignment through nonscalar intermediates and general N-dimensional deletion remain open.

features.feature: Transactional root-and-path lvalues across member, parenthesis, and brace segments
features.limits: Intermediate selections must resolve to one value. Missing roots can be seeded from the next path segment for numeric, Cell, or Struct indexed creation before transactional copy-back. HIR does not execute classdef objects; object setters and handle aliases retain their documented side effects; typed/native tiers fall back to the VM.

features.feature: Scoped global and per-function persistent bindings with reusable runtime sessions
features.limits: v0.78 requires declarations before use, initializes first declarations as 0-by-0 doubles, keys persistent variables by compiled callable identity plus canonical function identity, and routes all supported writes through RuntimeSessionState. Different modules may share globals without colliding same-named persistent functions. No-argument clear preserves shared state; the active v1.3 command form supports documented variable and pattern selectors while unsupported clear target categories remain explicit diagnostics. Individual state operations are mutex-protected, but callers must serialize compound invocation on one shared state. Typed/native regions fall back to the VM.

features.feature: Capability-gated eval, evalc, evalin, assignin, and current/caller/base workspace routing
features.limits: Character rows and string scalars can execute in the current, caller, or base workspace with zero or multiple outputs, evalc capture, catch expressions, nested evaluation, frame-transparent recursive caller/base routing, and projected dynamic source coordinates. Runtime workspace values introduced through initialWorkspace, assignin, or dynamic evaluation shadow same-named builtin/function bindings for ordinary, end, and colon indexing; nested callable arguments inherit an enclosing array's end context until a concrete shadowing array supplies a nearer target, and typed loops guard this precedence and fall back. Evaluated text inherits source-graph-visible local, nested, path, package, and private functions plus pre-existing module-bound handles. Direct calls, @name creation, permitted feval/str2func lookup, multiple outputs, captured workspace updates, evalc output, exceptions, recursive eval, and evalin caller routing synchronously delegate to the active owner engine; private aliases remain source scoped. Dynamic global declarations bind the selected frame to session globals; dynamic persistent declarations bind an ordinary non-static function identity and survive repeated compiled-session invocation. Script value use and static nested-workspace persistent declaration are rejected. Clear removes runtime associations without clearing underlying session state. HIR and explicit bytecode modes keep nested source on bytecode, while production mode inherits the guarded static Typed IR backend. Compile failure leaves the workspace unchanged; assignments and storage associations completed before an ordinary runtime error remain visible. Source is limited to 16 MiB and 1024 outputs and requires RuntimeSystemCapability::DynamicEvaluation. MATLAB R2024b itself rejects function and class definitions in eval; MParser reports them as unsupported dynamic definitions. Handles whose implementation is created by the temporary module cannot escape, while inherited owner handles may be invoked or returned and remain valid in their owner. Selected and ancestor workspaces, session global/persistent values, and reachable shared object fields are restored if temporary handles are stored in them.

features.feature: Canonical RuntimeValue ownership, shape, workspace, call-frame, and structured fallback contracts
features.limits: v0.79 freezes the internal source contract needed by the builtin registry: explicit ownership classes, storable transport boundaries, normalized shape/payload invariants, value-copy versus handle-alias behavior, function-handle identity/context lifetime, shared call-frame arity, and machine-readable fallback categories. v0.90 separately freezes its C ABI, C++ source API, and machine projection; internal C++ layout, garbage collection, and MATLAB type completeness are not public promises.

features.feature: Deterministic validation of internal bytecode before VM, optimization, or typed execution
features.limits: BytecodeProgram is an internal in-memory representation, not a public serialization or ABI. Direct untrusted entries validate on every call; CompiledModule and AdaptiveBytecodeVmSession paths own immutable snapshots and validate once before explicit trusted internal execution. Typed modules are installed only when each contract exactly matches the contract re-derived from validated bytecode.

features.feature: MException stack/cause/report contracts, throw policies, warning/lastwarn, assert, and embedding-visible diagnostics
features.limits: v0.73 exposes complete N-by-1 file/name/line stacks across the source graph, recursive causes, basic/extended reports, throwAsCaller, severity-tagged warnings, lastwarn, and assert. Active v1.3 development retains warning settings and lastwarn across one module session, clears them on session reset, isolates stateless calls, and shares them with nested evaluation. Correction is an explicit Missing placeholder and addCorrection reports MParser:UnsupportedExceptionCorrection; report text is MParser-defined, and typed/native tiers fall back to the VM.

features.feature: Named, anonymous, method, and built-in function handles with dynamic invocation
features.limits: v0.74 supports named, anonymous, and builtin handles in both baseline engines; method handles remain bytecode-only. feval, str2func, func2str, functions metadata, closure snapshots, same-CompiledModule persistence, and deterministic variable/path/package/private/builtin shadowing are covered. Active v1.3 anonymous root calls propagate implicit, zero, or explicit-one output context: zero-output callbacks preserve ans, while assigned calls retain output-count diagnostics. Anonymous text parsing, computed-string lazy source loading, serialization, and a cross-process handle ABI remain unsupported.

features.feature: classdef declarations, attributes, properties, methods, events, enumeration, arguments, and inheritance syntax
features.limits: The matrix declares supported attributes explicitly; undocumented attributes and every MATLAB metaclass edge are not implied.

features.feature: Value/handle construction, inheritance, superclass calls, access policy, and method dispatch
features.limits: v0.76 adds value, handle, and matlab.mixin.Heterogeneous arrays. Mixins beyond the declared subset, getDefaultScalarElement/convertObject hooks, ordinary class-dominance conversion, and every MATLAB constructor-order edge remain open.

features.feature: Validated, dependent, constant, abstract, observable, and accessor-backed properties
features.limits: v0.76 adds logical-order property comma-separated lists, whole-array method receivers, and indexed scalar value/handle copy-back. MATLAB-style direct nonscalar property assignment is rejected; general comma-separated assignment distribution and every MATLAB validation conversion class are not complete.

features.feature: Events, listeners, dynamic properties, explicit handle deletion, and validity
features.limits: v0.76 applies explicit delete and isvalid elementwise to handle arrays and skips repeated aliases. Active v1.3 listener invocation accepts anonymous wrappers whose root method has zero outputs without synthesizing a value. Automatic reachability destruction, cyclic collection, nonscalar event registration/notification, and every event-data subclass behavior remain open.

features.feature: Class, member, function, call-signature, argument, validation, namespace, and dynamic-property metadata queries
features.limits: v0.77 freezes the supported metadata graph, aliases, direct inheritance, class flags, public member lists, metadata-array projection, direct property-pair findobj filtering, property validation metadata/methods, module-bound validator handles, and dynamic-property defaults. Active v1.3 source loading recognizes literal class names passed to enumeration, events, methods, properties, meta.class.fromName, and matlab.metadata.Class.fromName; computed names remain dynamic. Descriptions remain empty; custom class aliases and InferiorClasses are not populated; GetMethod, SetMethod, and ArgumentValidator.Function reflection is incomplete; recursive handle-graph findobj options, metadata lifecycle events, direct metadata construction, HIR class execution, serialization, and the complete MATLAB metadata surface remain unsupported.

features.feature: Value, handle, and matlab.mixin.Heterogeneous object arrays with shared shape, indexing, mutation, transform, dispatch, and lifetime rules
features.limits: v0.76 covers scalar-fast and nonscalar storage, empty/logical/vector/N-dimensional indexing, transactional assignment and default-filled growth, deletion, concatenation/transforms, value copy-back, handle aliases and explicit lifecycle, property lists, whole-array methods, most-specific heterogeneous classes, display, equality, and guarded VM fallback. Active v1.3 enumeration queries return an N-by-1 same-class object array plus an N-by-1 names Cell. Default constructors currently run once per missing element; getDefaultScalarElement, convertObject, ordinary class conversion/dominance, custom indexing/concatenation overrides, automatic destruction, and a stable external object ABI remain open.

features.feature: Representative scalar math, reductions, scans, find, constructors, and array transforms
features.limits: The archived v1.2 catalog has 166 descriptors and 168 registered names. The v1.3 candidate catalog has 275 descriptors and 277 names after system, shared text/ordering/Cell/Struct, conversion, array callback, dense set, text-query, numeric/array/text-search/random utility, dynamic-workspace, stream-I/O, filesystem-management and metadata, MAT v5 persistence, and advanced-numeric tranches. Conversion coverage preserves exact int64/uint64 formatting and class roundtrips above flintmax, and cell2mat composes variable-segment rectangular N-dimensional block grids. Set coverage includes mixed numeric classes, exact wide-integer ordering, complex values, rows, stable/sorted ordering, Cell text, MATLAB NaN/missing non-membership, and payload-free value outputs when both operands are shaped missing arrays; generic missing mixes only with floating numeric classes and logical/index materialization is bounded to 10,000,000 elements. Advanced coverage includes statistics, dense linear algebra and matrix division, dot/cross, FFT/IFFT, convolution, integration, and polynomial fit/evaluation through one portable repository-owned C++20 backend. Core mathematical functions must remain repository-owned native C++20: Eigen is not linked or vendored and its source is not copied; external algorithms may inform an independently maintained implementation. Typed/native optimized regions retain guarded VM fallback. This is a coherent representative function train, not an unbounded MATLAB or toolbox count; rich-data, full regexp/Unicode and Pattern objects, legacy set modes, remote formats, extended MAT variants, recycle integration and broader platform attributes, extended GCD coefficients, broader decomposition/transform families, and long-tail overloads remain on the v1.x roadmap.

features.feature: Unified BuiltinRegistry, descriptors, call/result contract, and extension author rules
features.limits: Builtin source contract 1.1 remains the archived v1.2 integration contract. The v1.3 candidate contract 1.10 includes structured workspace/system/display context, caller output policy, synchronous RuntimeValue-callable dynamic invocation, execution-controlled utility, advanced-numeric, conversion, set, callback, and text-query handlers, current/caller/base resolution, source evaluation, corrected warning implicit-output metadata, shared stream-I/O, capability-bound filesystem management/metadata, MAT persistence, and dual file/object delete dispatch; its frozen snapshot has 275 descriptors and 277 names. This is a source-integration contract compiled with the engine, not a public C++ binary ABI or external native callback ABI. Intrinsics remain explicit engine operations; unsupported catalog entries remain deterministic.

features.feature: Capability-bound local path queries, metadata, whole-file text reads, temporary names, and filesystem mutation
features.limits: isfile and isfolder preserve string-array or character-cell shape and map missing strings to false. fileparts preserves character/string/cell containers without host access. fileread searches the current directory and session path, is bounded by the context read limit, and supports UTF-8 local files. tempname returns an unmaterialized candidate. mkdir, rmdir, copyfile, and movefile use zero-output diagnostics or up to three MATLAB-style status outputs, recursive directory handling, and basename wildcards. dir returns local display dates and MATLAB serial datenums. Text delete supports multiple filenames, string arrays, basename wildcards, and MATLAB-style missing-file/directory warnings while object deletion retains the VM lifecycle intrinsic. fileattrib queries platform-aware attributes and updates Windows a/h/s/w or UNIX w/x user scopes, including recursive updates that do not follow links. Rooted contexts validate source and destination and protect the root/current directory. Remote URLs, parent-component wildcards, selectable symbolic-link behavior, non-UTF-8 decoding, recycle integration, broader platform attributes, and link-race OS isolation remain unsupported.

features.feature: Resource-bounded MAT v5 workspace persistence through save and load
features.limits: Compressed and uncompressed MAT v5 files preserve all dense numeric classes, logical values, complex double/single arrays, UTF-16 character arrays, N-dimensional Cell arrays, and Struct arrays. The decoder accepts little- and big-endian tags, small data elements, compact numeric storage, and exact signed/unsigned 64-bit payloads. Zero-output load transactionally imports all or selected variables into the current workspace; one-output load returns a scalar Struct without mutation. Input, decompression expansion, decoded shape-driven allocations, value nesting, and compressed-element nesting are bounded. save supports the default compressed form, -v7, -mat, and -nocompression. MAT v4/v7.3, strict v6 output, append/ASCII modes, sparse/table/object values, String/missing values, function handles, and arbitrary object graphs are unsupported.

features.feature: Bytecode VM as the production semantic fallback for all legal target-subset code
features.limits: Features marked unsupported elsewhere in this matrix are not legal target-subset code.

features.feature: Guarded portable typed regions with transactional fallback
features.limits: Coverage is intentionally narrower than VM semantics; guard failure must fall back without partial mutation.

features.feature: Bundled SLJIT native scalar/branched/linear-array kernels on x64 and AArch64
features.limits: Native coverage is incremental and never blocks correct VM execution; SIMD and general matrices remain future work.

features.feature: Adaptive tiering, guarded invalidation, process-local native cache, and stateful module sessions
features.limits: RuntimeSessionState persists global and function-persistent bindings independently from adaptive profiling; adaptive reset does not erase it. v0.90 freezes the v1.0 cache as bounded and process-local and stress-tests concurrent compile, lookup, reconfiguration, clear, and accounting. Disk persistence remains additive until atomic storage, bounds, corruption recovery, and complete invalidation are implemented.

features.feature: Compile-once CompiledModule and repeated entry invocation from C++ or a narrow C host
features.limits: Engine-neutral stateless/persistent compile-once execution is projected through the v1.3 candidate C ABI generation 2 revision 1, C++ source API 1.3, and machine protocol 1.1 with failure/concurrency boundaries, relocated consumers, exact typed values, and guarded VM fallback. They do not expose internal RuntimeValue/VM layouts, promise a C++ binary ABI, or imply that every legal script is optimized.

features.feature: Engine-neutral module invocation request/result, staged diagnostics, backend selection, and execution summary
features.limits: The shared request/result behavior includes resource stops and protocol-1.1 CLI projection. Existing VM-specific invoke APIs remain internal development tools. C ABI generation 2 revision 1 and header-only C++ source API 1.3 expose no public C++ binary layout; their current declarations are frozen as v1.3 candidate source artifacts.

features.feature: Cooperative cancellation plus instruction, wall-time, call-depth, per-value array-payload, and diagnostic execution limits
features.limits: Instruction, deadline, and cancellation controls suppress current typed/native regions and use deterministic VM checkpoints. Call-depth, per-value recursive payload, and diagnostic limits preserve eligible optimized regions. Cancellation is cooperative; noncooperative blocking host code cannot be forcibly interrupted. Array bytes are not an aggregate process-heap/RSS cap, completed side effects are not rolled back, lock-admission wait is outside runtime wall time, the internal source API may throw bad_alloc, and the public C boundary maps it without publishing partial handles.

features.feature: Pure C shared-library ABI with opaque lifetimes, column-major values, diagnostics, sessions, resource controls, and module ownership
features.limits: The v1.3 candidate is C source API 1.3 over ABI generation 2 revision 1 with 117 exports. It transports exact typed/complex numeric and shaped-missing values, copied composite/text inputs, returned objects and handles, source metadata, output/results, immutable column-major views, resources, synchronization, failure containment, and a rooted system-context handle while retaining generation/SOVERSION 2. The released ABI 1.1 and archived v1.2 revision-0 snapshots remain historical evidence. Borrowed input buffers and an external native callback table remain future work.

features.feature: Pure C explicit/in-memory source graphs and UTF-8 entry/search-path loading with source metadata and stable load diagnostics
features.limits: Ordered source descriptors intentionally carry only names and source text. The v1.2 compile-with-options path additionally treats one in-memory unit as the entry and uses the production loader for package, private, path-precedence, and class-folder dependencies. Source names and paths must be valid UTF-8; loaded names are normalized filesystem identities. The active ABI 2 source-unit layout uses a fixed stride and is validated against current headers; compatibility with superseded development layouts is not retained.

features.feature: Installable relocatable C and C++20 SDKs with exported CMake API and CLI targets
features.limits: The relocatable package includes the C ABI, header-only C++ source API, CLI, protocol schema, public contract, metadata, examples, documentation, license, and notices. v1.0 emits platform/architecture ZIP or TGZ archives, SHA-256 files, and an unsigned in-toto Statement v1 with SLSA Provenance v1 metadata, then validates C11, multi-TU C++20, and CLI protocol use from an unpacked SDK. Tag v1.0.0 completed the final Sigstore operation in Actions run 30780391460; all five archives and five provenance statements have retained and independently verified bundles. The published 32-asset Release preserves those exact subject digests and has a retained canonical redownload audit.

features.feature: Versioned production CLI, strict option applicability, stable diagnostic mode names, and machine-channel separation
features.limits: CLI contract 1.0 freezes --run, --jit, invocation/source/cache options, machine selection, channel classes, and exits. Repeated single-value options and options in an inapplicable mode are rejected instead of ignored. Historical diagnostic mode names remain supported through v1.x, but their human formatting is not a machine protocol. The undocumented pre-v1 --run-interpreter alias was removed in favor of --run-hir.

features.feature: Versioned one-shot JSON result protocol over engine-neutral module execution
features.limits: Protocol 1.1 is the frozen v1.2 candidate wire contract. It carries explicit numeric-class metadata, exact JSON integers for every fixed-width integer class, separate imaginary data for complex double/single values, optional dimensions for shaped missing values, and optional ordered output-event/top-level-expression arrays while retaining one-shot execution, staged diagnostics, summaries, stable exits, recursive schema validation, and exact one-document stdout framing. The 1.1 minimal compatibility snapshot and 1.0 snapshot remain historical producer evidence; tolerant major-1 consumers accept the additive fields. Serialization failure uses a static exit-4 request-rejected record; an output-transport failure can still leave stdout missing or partial. Objects remain opaque, retained values require the C API, and this is not a persistent transport protocol.

features.feature: Current C API 1.3 and ABI generation/revision policy, caller-sized extensible roots, sealed fixed-stride records, and exact export validation
features.limits: C ABI generation 2 revision 1 is the v1.3 candidate with SOVERSION/install-name major 2, exact 64-bit layout checks, an immutable header snapshot, and 117 exports. It retains every archived v1.2 revision-0 symbol and layout while adding rooted system-context options, ownership, capability queries, and bound invocation/session entry points. Current and archived evidence plus in-repository/relocated consumers are validated independently.

features.feature: Header-only C++20 RAII SDK over the narrow C ABI with installed CMake consumption
features.limits: The v1.3 candidate header-only C++ source API 1.3 covers compile/load/invoke-many, in-memory loading with search paths, source metadata, synchronous output sinks, retained output/expression results, RAII ownership, every core numeric class, complex buffers, diagnostics, sessions, cancellation, resource summaries, documented concurrency, and RAII rooted SystemContext binding over C ABI revision 1 without exposing internal C++ layouts. It has no C++ binary ABI promise and is tested through current and relocated multi-translation-unit consumers. The v1.2 source API 1.2 snapshots remain archived evidence.

features.feature: Concurrent embedding lifecycle, module-bound mutable-graph synchronization, exact shared-library exports, and release-platform consumers
features.limits: Pure stateless calls remain concurrent. Requests carrying module-bound graphs serialize per owner, and every session operation from one module conservatively takes the same graph lock before its own session lock. Queue wait is outside runtime wall-time accounting. Host-created arrays remain copy-in with readonly value-owned output spans; external native callback tables and borrowed input buffers are Post-v1.0.

features.feature: Apache-2.0 project licensing, attribution, third-party notices, and installed package metadata
features.limits: MParser first-party source and documentation are licensed under Apache-2.0 with Copyright 2026 Wang Xin. Installed SDKs and release archives carry LICENSE, NOTICE, and third-party notices and expose checked metadata paths through CMake. Vendored components retain their own terms. SHA-256 records and unsigned SLSA provenance provide integrity and audit evidence; tag v1.0.0 adds accepted Sigstore authentication for all five archive/provenance pairs. The final hosted Release and post-publication download verification are complete.

features.feature: Host-routed display/formatted output, ordered retained output and top-level expression results, source classification, and in-memory production source loading
features.limits: Top-level results represent script expression statements; assignments are available through the workspace result instead. Suppressed expressions update ans and are retained without human display. disp plus the current stdout-only fprintf/sprintf subset supports diufFeEgGsc conversions, bounded static width/precision, Unicode text/code points, and repeated array formatting; file identifiers, dynamic width/precision, length modifiers, complex numeric conversion, and full MATLAB formatting remain outside this slice. Width is capped at 1 MiB, precision at 4096, and one formatted result at 16 MiB. Output callbacks are synchronous and must not re-enter the executing module/session.

features.feature: Public rooted runtime-system contexts with explicit host capabilities and retained session ownership
features.limits: The v1.3 candidate ABI generation 2 revision 1 adds a rooted native context, explicit capability bits, current/temporary/search directories, deterministic random seed, file limits, context-bound stateless execution, and retained session ownership while preserving the archived v1.2 revision-0 layouts and 109 exports. Path-oriented reads, creation, removal, copy, and move canonicalize the longest existing ancestor, validate both endpoints, reject resolved or symbolic-link escapes, and protect the root/current directory. Environment and process capabilities remain host-wide. The root is not an OS sandbox and cannot prevent a hostile local process racing link changes. Shared contexts intentionally share mutable path, random, and file state; legal optimized-ineligible calls retain VM fallback.

features.feature: Versioned current C/C++ source APIs, narrow C ABI, and machine-readable result protocol
features.limits: The v1.3 candidate contracts are CLI 1.0, C source API 1.3, C ABI generation 2 revision 1, header-only C++ source API 1.3, machine protocol 1.1, and builtin source contract 1.10. Frozen v1.2 and released v1 hashes, snapshots, provenance, authentication, and publication evidence remain archived and unchanged.

features.feature: Windows x64, Linux x64/ARM64, and macOS x64/ARM64 configure/build/test paths
features.limits: CI covers Windows x64, Linux x64, native Linux ARM64, macOS x64, and macOS ARM64. Actions run 30732814590 passed all seven execution jobs, including the native Linux ARM64 host check, full SLJIT suite, and accepted non-emulated ARM MIDR-labelled performance reports. Final tag run 30780391460 repeated all seven execution jobs and completed the five-platform authentication assembly. A separate AArch64 cross-build/QEMU lane validates native-JIT and portable fallback execution, installed consumers, and the release package without treating emulated timing as performance evidence.

features.feature: Optimized smoke executables retain executable assertions on MSVC, GCC, and Clang
features.limits: This protects current assert-based tests; new high-risk tests should prefer explicit failure helpers.

features.feature: Versioned parse, compile, process-cold, runtime, allocation, memory, binary-size, and native-cache baseline evidence
features.limits: The non-installed engineering collector emits protocol-1.0 raw timing/allocation samples, source/binary SHA-256 identities, and exact boundaries without machine-specific pass/fail thresholds. Allocation activity is not live heap, peak RSS is process-wide, process-cold is not filesystem-cache-cold, and emulated reports are functional evidence only. The native evidence target rejects emulation and unknown CPU identities while validating revision, platform, architecture, native cache behavior, and file identities before CI upload. Fixed Windows reports support the v1.x JIT-scope decision; Actions run 30691616946 adds accepted Windows/Linux/macOS x64 and native-architecture macOS ARM64 hosted-runner evidence, while run 30732814590 adds the accepted native Linux ARM64 ARM MIDR-labelled pair. Hosted ARM results are not bare-metal timing claims.

features.feature: Task-oriented v1 manuals, human support summary, migration policy, and executable CLI documentation consistency
features.limits: The prose routes users to versioned machine-readable authorities and distinguishes target platforms from current evidence. The documentation smoke derives frozen modes/options from CLI contract 1.0, checks live help, and executes human and JSON production samples. A release-readiness gate requires an empty open Must-have set and rejects any newly open Must-have that implies framework work.
